hero.text: In a short voice or video interview, Frank learns whether customers need what your higher plans offer, and what stops them from moving up: price, approval, unclear value or a missing feature. Then it ranks every reason by how many customers raised it.

what.sub: An upgrade barriers interview is a short conversation with a customer who has stayed on their current plan.
what.para: It finds out how they use the product today, whether they need more, and what stands between them and a higher plan.
what.quote: Your billing data shows who stays on the same plan and who hits plan limits. It doesn’t show whether they need more, whether they understand what the next plan offers, or who would have to approve the cost.

title: The upgrade barriers interview
research guide.
guide.sub: Upgrade barriers interviews generally follow a six-part guideline built to gather the verifiable insights you need. Every question is editable, and the AI Researcher helps you adapt the Research Guide to your product.
steps: How they use it today
The workflows they rely on, how many people use it, and how often.
Where the plan gets in the way
Moments when their current plan limits them, and how they work around it. Frank asks for a specific example.
What they know about higher plans
What they think the next plan includes, and whether that matches what it actually offers.
Whether they need more
Which features they would use, and what result they would get from them. Some customers don’t need more, and that’s worth knowing too.
What’s holding them back
Price, budget timing, an approval process, unclear value, or a feature that isn’t on any plan.
What would make them upgrade
The change in price, packaging or proof that would make the higher plan an easy decision.
guide.note: Frank doesn’t stop at the first answer. It follows up when a reply is vague and comes back to topics later in the conversation. That’s how “it’s too expensive” becomes “it’s worth it, but anything over $500 a month needs our CFO’s approval, and I can’t show the return yet.”
